title: Comparison table
subject: History
unit: Spring 1: The Titanic and polar exploration (Frozen Kingdom)
source: Seeded from history/y6 lesson 6 (Comparison table (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 6: Scott and Amundsen: the race to the South Pole. To understand the race to the South Pole and the reasons for its different outcomes

questions.q: How many weeks earlier did Amundsen arrive?
questions.a: About five weeks (14 December to 17 January)
questions.model: 14 December to 14 January is one month. Then 3 more days. About five weeks.

questions.q: Give one way Amundsen's methods were different.
questions.a: For example: he used skilled dog teams
A store of food and fuel left for the journey

questions.q: Core: Make a comparison table of the two expeditions (leader, country, transport, clothing, outcome).
questions.a: Amundsen: Norway, dogs and skis, fur, reached Pole first and returned safely. Scott: Britain, ponies, motors and man-hauling, wool and windproof cloth, reached Pole second and died on return.
questions.model: Teacher shows row 1: 'Leader and country: Amundsen, Norway; Scott, Britain.'

questions.q: Extend: Write a paragraph explaining why Amundsen succeeded. Use the portal response box.
questions.a: For example: Amundsen succeeded mainly because his dogs and skis were fast and he had many depots, while Scott's team had to haul their own sledges

questions.q: Stretch: Was Scott's failure bad luck or bad planning? Give your view.
questions.a: Reasoned view using weather, illness and planning choices

questions.q: Big question: why did Amundsen succeed and Scott's team die?
questions.a: Amundsen's dogs, skis, fur clothing and depots were better suited; Scott's team faced terrible weather and hauled their own sledges
